family.name: pp_fin
family.title: Extruded-fin heat sink: fin temperature over the design space

reference.name: 1-D fin theory on the fin-array resistance network
reference.citation: Incropera & DeWitt, Fundamentals of Heat and Mass Transfer, ch. 3 (fins); Elenbaas (1942) and Teertstra et al. (1999) for the convective coefficient; pinneapple_physics.closed_form.plate_fin_heatsink and .fin_array_conduction
assumptions: steady state, 1-D conduction along each fin with an adiabatic-tip corrected length
radiation neglected (the module says the part runs cooler than predicted in still air)
forced flow assumed ducted: all air passes between the fins
air properties from the module's own correlations, one iteration to convergence

split.policy: random by geometry, fixed by the seed: a held-out body is never a training body

ensemble_spread.note: standard deviation between the bagged ensemble heads, not a confidence level

probes.name: a 30-fin sink: 3x the fin count of the trained family
a 15x-power sink: 450 W on a 3 cm fin
reasons: operating parameters [0] outside the trained range

ood.threshold: the library's own: geometry-code distance over the 95th percentile of the training nearest-neighbour distances, above 1.5x
ood.note: reported as measured: a probe the model does not flag is not thereby inside its validity domain

measured_here: held-out relative L2 0.5612 on 4 designs of 428 points, tolerance 0.05
constant-field baseline on the same designs: 0.5565
OOD: 1/2 probes outside the family flagged, 2/4 held-out designs flagged
not_measured: the reference itself: analytic — 1-D fin theory on the fin-array resistance network, with the assumptions it lists
agreement with a solver or with measured data for any geometry of this family
whether the ensemble spread is calibrated: it is the spread between bootstrap heads
behaviour outside the declared geometry and operating bounds of the family
